title: Triviality on fibres
statement:
Let $P$ be a proper geometrically integral $k$-scheme, let $T$ be a
$k$-scheme of finite type, let $f:P\times T\to T$ be the projection,
and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $P\times T$. For $t\in T$
write $P_t=P\times_k\kappa(t)$ and $\mathcal L_t=\mathcal L|_{P_t}$.

1. **(1)** $\mathcal L_t$ is trivial if and only if $H^0(P_t,\mathcal L_t)\ne0$
  and $H^0(P_t,\mathcal L_t^{-1})\ne0$.
1. **(2)** The set of $t\in T$ such that $\mathcal L_t$ is trivial is closed.
1. **(3)** If $\mathcal L$ is trivial on $P\times U_\alpha$ for an open
  cover $(U_\alpha)$ of $T$, then $\mathcal L\simeq f^*\mathcal M$ with $\mathcal M=f_*\mathcal L$
  invertible.

steps.text:
Since $P$ is proper and geometrically integral, so is $P_t$ over
$\kappa(t)$, and $H^0(P_t,\mathcal O_{P_t})=\kappa(t)$
(Stacks [0BUG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BUG)).
For (1), let $s$ and $s'$ be nonzero sections of $\mathcal L_t$ and
$\mathcal L_t^{-1}$. Since $P_t$ is integral, the product $ss'$ is a
nonzero element of $H^0(P_t,\mathcal O)=\kappa(t)$, hence a unit, and
so $s$ vanishes nowhere. The converse is clear. For (2), the functions
$t\mapsto\dim H^0(P_t,\mathcal L_t^{\pm1})$ are upper semicontinuous
(Stacks [0BDN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BDN)), so the loci where they are positive are closed, and (1)
identifies their intersection with the set in question. For (3), the
morphism $f$ is proper and flat with geometrically integral fibres, so
$f_*\mathcal O_{P\times T}=\mathcal O_T$ (Stacks [0E0L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E0L)). On $P\times U_\alpha$ we have $\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal O$,
so $f_*\mathcal L$ is invertible on $U_\alpha$ and the adjunction map
$f^*f_*\mathcal L\to\mathcal L$ is an isomorphism there.
